1.overview: After Moses’s death, the LORD commissions Joshua to lead Israel across the Jordan, promises him the land and divine presence, and commands him to obey the law with courage. Joshua orders the people to prepare for the crossing, directs the eastern tribes to help their fellow Israelites take the land, and receives their pledge of obedience and support.

2.overview: Joshua sends two spies from Shittim to Jericho, where Rahab hides them from the king’s men and declares her belief that the LORD has given Israel the land. She secures a promise to spare her family, helps the spies escape, and marks her house with a scarlet cord; the spies return to Joshua and report that the people of the land fear Israel.

sections.heading: Rahab Seeks Protection for Her Family
The Escape and the Scarlet Cord

3.overview: Israel leaves Shittim and camps at the Jordan, where officers direct the people to follow the ark at a distance; Joshua tells them to consecrate themselves and sends the priests ahead. The LORD promises to establish Joshua and drive out the Canaanite nations, and the Jordan’s waters stop when the priests carrying the ark enter it, allowing all Israel to cross on dry ground opposite Jericho.

4.overview: The Israelites take twelve stones from the Jordan for a memorial at their camp in Gilgal, while Joshua also sets twelve stones where the priests stood in the river. After the priests carrying the ark leave the Jordan, its waters return, and Joshua explains that the stones will remind future generations of Israel’s crossing and the LORD’s mighty power.

sections.heading: Twelve Stones Taken from the Jordan
The Crossing Ends and the Waters Return

5.overview: The Amorite and Canaanite kings fear Israel after hearing of the Jordan crossing, while Joshua circumcises the wilderness-born generation at Gilgal, where Israel keeps Passover and begins eating Canaan’s produce as the manna ceases. Near Jericho, Joshua encounters the Commander of the LORD’s army, who declares the ground holy.

sections.heading: Passover and the End of Manna
The Commander of the LORD’s Army

6.overview: The LORD gives Jericho to Joshua and directs Israel to march around the city with the ark and priests sounding rams’ horns, then shout on the seventh day. The walls collapse, Israel captures and destroys the city while sparing Rahab and her family and placing the metals in the LORD’s treasury, and Joshua pronounces a curse on anyone who rebuilds Jericho as the LORD establishes his fame.

7.overview: After Achan takes items devoted to destruction, Israel is defeated at Ai, and Joshua appeals to the LORD, who reveals that Israel’s disobedience has caused the defeat. The LORD directs Israel to identify the offender, Achan confesses and the stolen goods are found, and he and his household are put to death in the Valley of Achor, after which the LORD’s anger turns away.

sections.heading: Achan’s theft and Israel’s defeat at Ai
Joshua’s appeal and the LORD’s instruction
Achan’s punishment in the Valley of Achor

8.overview: The LORD directs Joshua to use an ambush to capture Ai, and Israel defeats its forces, takes the city, and carries off its livestock and plunder. At Mount Ebal, Joshua builds an altar, inscribes the law on stones, and reads its blessings and curses before all Israel.

sections.heading: The Law Is Read at Mount Ebal

9.overview: The kings west of the Jordan unite against Israel, while the Gibeonites disguise themselves as envoys from a distant land and secure a treaty from Joshua and Israel’s leaders, who do not seek the LORD’s counsel. When Israel discovers that Gibeon and its neighboring towns are nearby, the leaders honor their oath and make the Gibeonites woodcutters and water carriers for the congregation and the LORD’s altar.

10.overview: Adoni-zedek and four Amorite kings attack Gibeon, and Joshua marches from Gilgal to its defense; the LORD routs the armies, sends hailstones, and, in response to Joshua’s appeal, the sun and moon stand still until Israel completes the victory. Joshua captures and kills the five kings, then conquers Makkedah, Libnah, Lachish, Eglon, Hebron, and Debir, taking the surrounding region before returning to Gilgal.

sections.heading: The Amorite Alliance and Israel’s Victory

11.overview: Jabin of Hazor gathers northern kings and peoples at the waters of Merom, where Joshua’s army defeats them and destroys their horses and chariots as the LORD commands. Joshua captures Hazor and other cities, takes the land from Mount Halak to Baal-gad, defeats the Anakim except in Gaza, Gath, and Ashdod, and assigns the land to Israel’s tribes, after which the land rests from war.

12.overview: The chapter recounts the lands east of the Jordan conquered by Moses and assigned to Reuben, Gad, and half of Manasseh, listing Sihon and Og as the defeated kings. It then lists the western lands conquered by Joshua and Israel and names the thirty-one kings defeated there.

sections.heading: Kings and Lands East of the Jordan
The Thirty-One Kings of the West

13.overview: The LORD tells the aged Joshua that much land remains unconquered and directs him to allot it to the nine tribes and half-tribe of Manasseh. The chapter records the eastern inheritances Moses assigned to Reuben, Gad, and half of Manasseh, and states that the LORD is Levi’s inheritance.

14.overview: Eleazar, Joshua, and the tribal heads oversee the division of Canaan, with the nine and a half tribes receiving land west of the Jordan and the Levites receiving cities and pasturelands rather than a tribal allotment. Caleb recalls Moses’ promise at Kadesh-barnea, asks Joshua for the hill country, and receives Hebron as his inheritance.

15.overview: Joshua assigns Judah its boundaries and records Caleb’s inheritance at Hebron, his defeat of Anak’s descendants, and Othniel’s capture of Debir, after which Caleb gives Acsah the upper and lower springs. The chapter lists Judah’s cities by region and notes that Judah’s descendants do not drive the Jebusites from Jerusalem, where they continue to live among them.

16.overview: The allotment for Joseph’s descendants is described, and Ephraim and Manasseh receive their inheritance, with Ephraim’s borders and cities detailed. Ephraim’s territory includes cities within Manasseh’s inheritance, while the Canaanites in Gezer remain as forced laborers.

17.overview: Manasseh’s allotment includes land east of the Jordan, shares for Zelophehad’s daughters, and territories bordered by Ephraim, Asher, and Issachar; the tribe does not fully displace the Canaanites from several assigned cities. When the house of Joseph asks for more land because of its population, Joshua directs it to clear the hill country and says it can drive out the Canaanites despite their iron chariots.

sections.heading: Joshua’s Response to the House of Joseph

18.overview: Israel assembles at Shiloh, where the Tent of Meeting is set up, and Joshua directs the seven tribes without allotments to survey the land before he distributes it by lot. The chapter records Benjamin’s assigned boundaries and lists its cities and villages.

19.overview: The lots assign territories to Simeon, Zebulun, Issachar, Asher, Naphtali, and Dan, with Simeon’s towns lying within Judah’s inheritance and Dan later capturing Leshem and renaming it. After the tribal allotments are completed at Shiloh, the Israelites give Joshua Timnath-serah in Ephraim, and Eleazar, Joshua, and the family heads finish distributing the land by lot.

sections.heading: Joshua’s Inheritance and the Completed Allotments

20.overview: The LORD instructs Joshua to establish cities of refuge for people who kill unintentionally, where they receive protection and remain until trial and the death of the high priest. Israel designates six cities across the land for Israelites and foreigners, so an accidental manslayer can escape the avenger of blood until standing trial before the assembly.

sections.heading: Instructions for the Cities of Refuge

21.overview: At Shiloh, the Levites ask Eleazar, Joshua, and Israel’s tribal leaders for the cities and pasturelands commanded through Moses, and Israel assigns forty-eight cities among the Kohathite, Gershonite, and Merarite clans. The chapter concludes that the LORD gives Israel the land and rest he promised, and that none of his promises fail.

sections.heading: The Levites request and receive cities
Cities for the other Levite clans

22.overview: Joshua commends and releases the Reubenites, Gadites, and half-tribe of Manasseh to return across the Jordan after their service, and they build a large altar near the river. Israel prepares for war, but a delegation led by Phinehas hears that the altar is intended as a witness of shared worship, and the tribes are reconciled.

23.overview: As Israel’s leader grows old, Joshua summons its leaders and recalls how the LORD has fought for Israel and allotted the remaining land. He urges Israel to keep the Law and hold fast to the LORD, warning that association with other nations and worship of their gods will bring judgment, despite the LORD’s fulfilled promises.

sections.heading: Joshua recalls the LORD’s victories and land allotment
Joshua warns against idolatry and compromise

24.overview: At Shechem, Joshua recounts the LORD’s guidance of Israel from Abraham through the conquest and calls the people to choose whom they will serve; Israel pledges service, and Joshua establishes a covenant with witnesses. The chapter records Joshua’s death and burial, Israel’s continued service during the elders’ lifetimes, Joseph’s burial at Shechem, and Eleazar’s death and burial.

sections.heading: The LORD’s acts in Israel’s history
Israel renews the covenant at Shechem
